remaining_limitations: NumPy dtype annotations do not statically encode shape, units, finiteness or mathematical assumptions.
Heterogeneous model metadata and advanced provider options are explicit object-valued mappings; callers narrow model-specific payloads.
Some class methods rely on inferred types; private dynamic provider code retains localized Any; the configured Pyright mode is basic, not strict.
Original numerical-audit branch coverage was not remeasured for this contract follow-up.
User callbacks, ill-conditioned problems, model identification and uncertainty calibration require application-specific validation.
Scenario measure provenance is an assertion; P to Q transformations are explicit and require valid assumptions.
Arbitrary callbacks/native handles have no universal portable serialization or cross-provider-version reproducibility guarantee.
Validation concerns the recorded Python 3.14 quant dependencies; other Python versions and hardware/provider matrices are outside scope.
